{{Short description|Australian chemist and lichenologist (1931–1978)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
{{Use Australian English|date=December 2021}}

'''Geoffrey Charles Bratt''' (8 January 1931 – 16 October 1977)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bratt, Geoffrey |url=https://eoas.info/biogs/P007581b.htm |access-date=2025-07-15 |website=Encyclopedia of Australian Science and Innovation |language=en-gb}}</ref> was an Australian chemist and [[lichenologist]].

==Life and career==
Bratt was born in [[Hobart, Tasmania]]. In 1952, he earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in [[applied chemistry]] from the [[University of Tasmania]]. That year, he started working at the [[EZ Industries|Electrolytic Zinc Company]] as a research scientist. He held this position for three years before leaving to enter the [[Imperial College of Science]] in London to start a [[PhD]] degree. He completed this in 1959 and thereafter returned to the Electrolytic Zinc Company, again as a research scientist; by the time of his death he was the Senior Principle Research Officer. He investigated methods of purification and [[electroplating|electrodeposition]] of [[zinc]], and published several [[patent]]s regarding this and the purification and recovery of other metals.<ref name="Filson 1978"/>

As a result of his lifelong interest in [[bushwalking]], Bratt joined the Imperial College Exploring Society Karakorum Expedition conducted in 1957–58, the aim of which was to scale the world's [[K2|second-highest mountain peak]]. Although the expedition did not climb this peak, they did manage to successfully climb [[Saltoro Kangri|K10]]. As a member of the [[International Glaciological Society|British Glaciological Society]] he accepted an invitation from [[Eric Shipton]] to join an expedition to [[Patagonia]] in 1958–59. It was here that he met lichenologist [[Peter Wilfred James]], who stimulated his interest in lichens. After returning to Australia, he set up a [[herbarium]] in his home in [[West Moonah]], and added many lichens to his [[scientific collection|collections]] from numerous bushwalking trips in Tasmania. After suffering [[kidney failure]] in 1974, he had to forgo major expeditions, but he was able to spend more time with the specimens in his herbarium, and most of his lichen publications were published after that.<ref name="Filson 1978"/>

==Memberships and awards==
* member of the [[Royal Geographical Society]] in 1959<ref name="Filson 1978"/>
* life membership of the [[Royal Society of Tasmania]] in 1965<ref name="Filson 1978"/>
* appointed Honorary Research Associate in the Department of Botany at the University of Tasmania in 1969<ref name="Filson 1978"/>
* Hofmann Prize for extractive metallurgy in 1971 (shared with R.W. Pickering)<ref name="Filson 1978"/>

==Eponyms==
Several lichen [[taxon|taxa]] have been named to honour Bratt. These include ''[[Cladonia enantia]]'' var. ''brattii'' {{small|Kantvilas (2013)}};<ref name="Kantvilas 2013"/> ''[[Menegazzia brattii]]'' {{small|Kantvilas (2012)}};<ref name="Kantvilas 2012"/> ''[[Parmelia brattii]]'' {{small|Essl. (1976)}};<ref name="Culberson & Esslinger 1976"/>  ''[[Pseudocyphellaria brattii]]'' {{small|D.J.Galloway & Kantvilas (1997)}};<ref name="Galloway 1997"/> ''[[Rinodina brattii]]'' {{small|H.Mayrhofer (1984)}};<ref name="Mayrhofer 1984"/> and ''[[Vouauxiomyces brattii]]'' {{small|S.Y.Kondr. (1996)}}.<ref name="Kondratyuk 1996"/>
